title: Health, pharmacy and emergencies
intro: Read plate 3 and unit 9 first for the body itself. This unit is what you say when something is wrong. The single most useful sentence here is me duele — see unit 9.

entries.note: la droguería in Colombia. In much of Latin America pharmacies sell far more without prescription than in Europe.

ex.en: Is there a pharmacy nearby?

entries.note: One word for both. Context does all the work.

ex.en: I need a prescription for this.

ex.es: Me dio la receta de su abuela.
ex.en: She gave me her grandmother's recipe.

entries.note: el medicamento is the formal word for a drug; la inyección an injection.

ex.es: Toma una pastilla cada ocho horas.
ex.en: Take one tablet every eight hours.

entries.note: enfermarse is to fall ill; el enfermero the nurse.

ex.en: It's a common illness here.

entries.note: el resfriado is a cold. Latin America also says la gripa.

ex.en: He was in bed with flu.

entries.note: toser is to cough. estornudar is to sneeze.

ex.en: She's had a cough since Sunday.

entries.note: herirse is to injure oneself; lastimarse the everyday version in Latin America.

ex.en: The wound needs cleaning.

entries.note: sangrar is to bleed. el análisis de sangre is a blood test.

ex.es: Le tomaron una muestra de sangre.
ex.en: They took a blood sample.

entries.note: romperse un hueso is to break a bone. Not to be confused with el oso, bear.

ex.es: Se rompió un hueso del pie.
ex.en: He broke a bone in his foot.
She has very sensitive skin.
It's a leather jacket.

entries.note: dolor de garganta is a sore throat.

ex.es: Me duele la garganta al tragar.
ex.en: My throat hurts when I swallow.

entries.note: el dentista treats both. dolor de muelas is toothache.

ex.es: Al bebé le salió el primer diente.
ex.en: The baby got his first tooth.
They took out one of my back teeth.

entries.note: Not la fecha, which is a calendar date — see unit 16.

ex.es: Tengo cita con el médico a las cuatro.
ex.en: I have a doctor's appointment at four.
They went on a first date.

ex.es: Empezó con una cita de Borges.
ex.en: She began with a quotation from Borges.

entries.note: la sala de emergencias or urgencias is the A&E department.

ex.en: Call the emergency services.

ex.es: La ambulancia llegó en diez minutos.
ex.en: The ambulance arrived in ten minutes.

entries.note: estar seguro is to be sure; el seguro médico is health insurance.

ex.en: Do you have health insurance?

ex.es: Estoy seguro de que lo vi.
ex.en: I'm sure I saw it.

entries.note: peligroso is dangerous. ¡Peligro! on a sign.

ex.en: He's out of danger.

entries.note: ¡Cuidado! is the universal watch out. cuidar is to look after.

ex.en: He needs special care.
Watch out, there's a car coming!

entries.note: sano of a person, saludable of food and habits.

ex.en: He eats healthily and sleeps well.

entries.note: ¡Que te mejores! is get well soon. empeorar is to get worse.

ex.en: I hope you get better soon.
